# Component map

## Current scope and verified state

This map describes the **Mirket** repository at `/Users/nazmi/Projects/skills`, whose distributable package is `plugins/mirket/`. The latest verified inventory is dated **November 11, 2026**.

- **Source:** Mirket **0.4.0**, with exactly **25 original natively authored skills**. The source package contains **76 files**.
- **Installed:** Normal Codex CLI **0.167.0** and Claude Code **2.1.311** installations both report Mirket **0.4.0**. Their installed caches match all **76 source files byte-for-byte**, with no missing, extra, or changed files.
- **Codex activation:** The installed plugin reports **25 skills** and four trusted active hooks: `PreToolUse`, `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, and `Stop`. No forged trust hashes or trust bypass are used.
- **Claude activation:** Startup exposed `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, and 25 skills. Authenticated model behavior, `Stop`, and `PreToolUse` enforcement remain unverified because Claude is not logged in. Hook activation and model adherence are separate evidence.
- **Public plugin release:** The verified 0.4.0 source and installed copies had **not** been committed, pushed, or publicly released as of November 11, 2026. Therefore 0.4.0 must not be described as the public plugin release.
- **Public website:** The separate Mirket website is deployed at `https://skills.mirket.dev/`. That deployment is a distinct website state and does not establish that the unreleased 0.4.0 plugin package was publicly released.

The current source and installed manifest layout is `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` for Codex and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` for Claude Code. There is **no portable root `plugin.json`** in the current source or installed caches. The Codex descriptor exposes `./skills/` and `./hooks/hooks.json`.

## Mirket plugin package

The package at `plugins/mirket/` is a reusable skill plugin for Codex and Claude Code. Its current internal structure is:

- `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` — current Codex descriptor and package metadata; it exposes `./skills/` and `./hooks/hooks.json`.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — Claude Code package metadata.
- `skills/` — the 25 packaged workflow skills. A packaged skill is the central catalog entity: its lowercase skill directory contains Markdown guidance, and `agents/openai.yaml` supplies skill metadata used by the repository catalog and website.
- `references/` — shared routing and other cross-skill references. The current routing reference is `plugins/mirket/references/Routing.md`; current reference filenames use PascalCase. Lowercase `routing.md` is historical rather than a current link.
- `assets/` — package branding.
- `hooks/` — Python lifecycle integrations.

Both marketplace integration files, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, point to the same Mirket package. The repository therefore has one distributable package with two host-facing marketplace integrations rather than separate Codex and Claude skill implementations.

The package covers project understanding, planning, engineering quality, design, communication, coordination, security, migration, release, deployment, and operations. Browser-oriented workflows do not include a bundled browser component; they require an available host capability.

## Active skill catalog and ownership boundaries

The latest inventory supports a **25-skill catalog**. The following names and boundaries are explicitly supported by the current source or the November 11 inventory; this is not an assertion that the list below is an exhaustive transcription of all 25 names.

- **Secure** — owns security and privacy.
- **Migrate** — owns changes to persistent state.
- **Release** — owns versioned artifacts and distribution. It does **not** own environment deployment.
- **Deploy** — owns environment rollout and activation.
- **Operate** — owns service health and recovery.
- **Focus** — includes the shipped-outcome review branch in the current lifecycle documentation.
- **Distill** — owns routine communication and concise, result-first communication behavior.
- **Author** — owns durable documents, substantive product copy, and issue triage. It is not the owner of routine replies.
- **Plan** — creates plans. Small work may use a compact plan; substantial work retains three planning files. The plan records authorization in its own Agreement section.
- **Orchestrate** — coordinates delegated work, selects task-appropriate workers and reasoning effort, checks results according to risk, and retains bounded root integration after workers hand ownership back. Independent review remains required when the task calls for it; inline work is not independent review.
- **Curate** — expands a known comparison only when the expansion is material and within scope.
- **Design** — is the design-director entry point for product UI, websites, illustration, brand systems, motion, slides, and generative artwork. It routes into focused references and hands implementation-oriented work to the appropriate design workflow.
- **Imagine** and **Critique** — remain distinct design responsibilities. Imagine’s picker makes implementation optional; Critique evaluates work during implementation and before delivery, requiring evidence for visual and performance claims.
- **Clean** — performs the applicable cleanup and review work within the intended scope, preserves files of uncertain purpose, corrects task-related stale guidance only when evidence supports the replacement, and uses a verified recovery copy before authorized removal of important hard-to-recreate work.
- **Equip** — compares keeping, adjusting, piloting, or switching when a working choice is a poor fit, then guides an authorized change through a representative check.
- **Adapt** — investigates only enough to understand missing or stale context, remains read-only during orientation, and proceeds directly to an already authorized fix.
- **Brief** and **Sleep** — support handoff and pause/resume coordination. Brief keeps handoffs actionable and exposes stale-context discrepancies; Sleep captures current knowledge and critical handoff state, safely stops task-owned agents while reporting ongoing operations, does not stop persistent services, and avoids creating a handoff when no work is pending unless explicitly requested.

The durable ownership rule is therefore one owner per outcome: security/privacy belongs to Secure; persistent state to Migrate; versioned artifacts/distribution to Release; rollout/activation to Deploy; health/recovery to Operate; routine communication to Distill; and durable documents, substantive copy, and issue triage to Author.

The routing convention is defined by `plugins/mirket/references/Routing.md` together with each packaged skill’s trigger description. The `plugins/mirket/hooks/distill.py` SessionStart behavior exposes the one-owner rule and the exact routing-reference path, and key packaged skills link to that guide. This current source behavior supersedes the older description of an undiscoverable routing gap for working-tree and installed-state audits; live semantic adherence by the model is still a separate verification question.

## Lifecycle hooks and host integration

Mirket’s hook subsystem is implemented in Python under `plugins/mirket/hooks/` and integrates the package with host lifecycle events.

- `SessionStart` exposes the routing guidance and one-owner rule.
- `UserPromptSubmit` supplies prompt-time guidance, including Distill behavior.
- `Stop` participates in final-review behavior.
- `Bash PreToolUse` performs the package’s pre-commit and Git-safety checks.

Hook commands run in Python isolated mode with five-second manifest timeouts. In the current working-tree behavior, `plugins/mirket/hooks/cleanup.py` is neutral by default and activates final review only when `MIRKET_FINAL_REVIEW=1`. With final review enabled and `stop_hook_active` false, it may request continuation; the blanket claim that it never requests another continuation is therefore too broad.

The cleanup hook also contains the repository-safety behavior for staged `.work/` files. Its current design uses a trusted Git executable, fixed probe arguments, read-only index inspection with external helpers disabled, preservation of quoted punctuation when detecting compound commands, and explicit handling of modes such as `git commit -a` and path-based commits. These are package responsibilities, not claims about Git’s implementation.

Codex hook discovery was corrected by adding `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` beside the Claude descriptor and removing the portable root `plugin.json`. The current installed Codex evidence confirms discovery and trust of all four hooks. Claude’s startup evidence confirms only the events and skills exposed before authenticated model behavior could be tested.

## Website and documentation subsystem

`website/` is a separate static Next.js documentation and discovery application for Mirket. It consumes repository content rather than maintaining a separate skill catalog.

- `website/lib/content.ts` reads repository Markdown and `agents/openai.yaml` skill metadata at build time.
- `website/components/RepoMarkdown.tsx` renders repository Markdown and maps repository links to local documentation routes or GitHub.
- `website/lib/discovery.ts` centralizes public-page discovery and the shared `PageInfo` model, including canonical path, title, description, and social-card fields.
- `website/data/workflows.json` feeds the workflow visualization component.
- `website/scripts/generate-diagrams.mjs` writes SVG diagrams into `docs/diagrams/`.
- `website/next.config.ts` produces deployable static files in `website/out/`.

Skill routes are constrained to generated `/docs/skills/<slug>/` pages, so unknown slugs do not create arbitrary dynamic pages. Each `SKILL.md` supplies a detail page, packaged skill metadata supplies homepage cards, and repository Markdown is also rendered so the GitHub and website documentation share the same source material.

The site generates documentation and adjacent-skill navigation, source-aware Markdown links, responsive workflow diagrams, reduced-motion static presentations, canonical metadata, JSON-LD, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, `llms.txt`, and versioned 1200-by-630 social PNGs. The current documentation inventory describes **28 indexable pages** for the 25-skill catalog.

The homepage contains the “How it Works” diagrams below the installer. The diagrams and mascot animation honor the system reduced-motion preference and have no individual playback controls or footer motion setting. The public deployment verified 23 live pages and 23 preview images for the deployed website state.

## Optional memory subsystem in this repository

The repository also contains an optional project-memory integration under `memory/`. It is separate from the plugin’s skill runtime and stores runtime configuration and memory data outside the repository.

- `memory/install.py` installs or rewires the configured integration.
- `memory/project_registry.py` binds hooks, MCP, and survey workers to project banks and recovers project identity and session bindings.
- `memory/doctor.py` inspects configuration, coverage, and freshness and supports bounded page refresh.
- `memory/test_*.py` covers the optional memory integration.

The subsystem provides directory-based bank isolation, session binding, survey and configuration adapters, diagnostics, freshness checks, and bounded refresh. Its current verification establishes project routing and queryability, not instantaneous page consistency: raw capture and recall can be current while background knowledge-page consolidation remains asynchronous. Runtime configuration and storage are intentionally outside the repository.

The current wiring uses a project-only freshness profile for `coding-agent::desktop-skills` with `surveyRefreshCommits=1`, `pageTriggerType=auto-refresh`, and `pageRefreshEveryTurns=1`; capture scope was unchanged. The repository’s memory work preserves existing working-tree revisions while addressing configuration preservation, canonical bank migration, diagnostics, freshness, recovery, and explicit verification boundaries.

## Repository support modules and verification material

- `tests/` covers hooks, distribution wiring, and behavioral-fixture preparation.
- `memory/test_*.py` covers the optional memory integration.
- `docs/` contains the main guide, diagrams, and decision records.
- `README.md` introduces installation and features.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents repository checks.
- `docs/decisions/` is the current location for settled ADRs. `plugins/mirket/skills/architect/SKILL.md` initializes this directory for the first settled ADR when it does not exist.
- `.work/decisions/` is reserved for private notes and drafts, not settled ADRs.

## State boundaries and verification limits

The strongest current package evidence is source plus byte-for-byte installed-cache comparison. It supports describing Mirket 0.4.0 as active in the normal Codex and Claude installations, but not as a public plugin release or as a deployed plugin revision.

The website has a separate public deployment at `https://skills.mirket.dev/`, replacing its former local-only static-export status. That deployment was validated with a clean static-site build, public HTTPS checks, and browser smoke tests. Website deployment evidence must not be used to infer that the current 0.4.0 plugin source was published or that every current working-tree hook behavior is deployed there.

Claude’s authenticated model behavior remains unverified because Claude is not logged in. Likewise, hook activation evidence does not prove model adherence to every skill or routing rule. The memory bank is queryable and has current verified findings, but asynchronous page synthesis is not proven instantaneous and sync status alone does not prove comprehensive survey or conversation coverage.

## Historical states and superseded architecture

- **November 8, 2026:** Mirket’s earlier published and installed states included 0.2.0 and 0.2.2, with earlier 20-skill and 43-skill descriptions. Those catalogs are not the current package and are retained only as history.
- **November 10, 2026:** Mirket 0.2.0’s published Design architecture used one `plugins/mirket/skills/design/SKILL.md` with ten selectable references. The earlier proposed five mandatory `design-*` stage skills were explicitly not part of that published package and are not current architecture.
- **November 10, 2026:** The website was first established as a local static-export Next.js application under `website/`; it was subsequently publicly deployed at `https://skills.mirket.dev/`, so the former local-only status is obsolete.
- **November 11, 2026:** The earlier portable-root-manifest layout was superseded. Current source and installed caches use `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, with no root `plugin.json`.
- **November 11, 2026:** The earlier convention placing settled ADRs in `.work/decisions` was superseded. Settled ADRs now belong in `docs/decisions/`; `.work/decisions/` is for private notes and drafts.
- **November 11, 2026:** The earlier default Stop-continuation description was superseded by neutral-by-default `plugins/mirket/hooks/cleanup.py`; final review is opt-in through `MIRKET_FINAL_REVIEW=1`, subject to `stop_hook_active`.
- **November 11, 2026:** The separate provenance manifest `plugins/mirket/sources.json` was removed from the working tree, and references to it were removed. It is not part of the current packaging layout.
- The bundled `agent-browser` component was removed from Mirket in the earlier 0.2.2 history. It is not an active Mirket component; browser workflows depend on an available host capability instead.
